title: Compact-support exchange isomorphism for geometric Frobenius
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite coefficient field $E/\Ql$ in $\Qlb$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ with the rational/common-stage Weil-complex categories of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $X_0,Y_0$ be finite-type $k_0$-schemes and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated and of finite type; put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $g_X,g_Y$ be the geometric-Frobenius automorphisms. For every domain of bounded constructible objects on which the compact-support direct image and the displayed pullbacks are defined, the compact-support base-change exchange of [def-exchange-projection] for the Cartesian semilinear square $fg_X=g_Yf$,
$$
\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg_Y^*Rf_!\longrightarrow Rf_!Lg_X^*,
$$
is a natural isomorphism. This holds after rationalization over $E$ and after passage to the common-stage $\Qlb$ category, with the coefficient-category and finite-Tor hypotheses of the underlying operations retained; no separatedness of $X_0$ or $Y_0$ is required.

source.place: Proof sentence 1: equivariant compact-support exchange along the geometric-Frobenius square

proof.text: By [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian], the displayed square commutes and is Cartesian, and both horizontal maps are scheme isomorphisms. Choose the compactification $c=(j,p)$ used to represent the exchange in [def-exchange-projection], and its base change $c'=(j',p')$ to the bottom-left copy of $Y$. Write $b:\overline X'=\overline X\times_{Y,g_Y}Y\to\overline X$ for its horizontal projection. It is an isomorphism: its inverse is the pair $(1_{\overline X},g_Y^{-1}p)$, and the two composites are identities by the fibre-product projections. The upper open square has horizontal arrows $b$ and $g_X$ after the Frobenius Cartesian identification. To use [def-exchange-projection] take $S=Y$, with structure maps $f:X\to Y$, $1_Y:Y\to Y$, and $g_Y:Y\to Y$ at the three original corners. Then $f$ and $g_Y$ are $S$-morphisms, separated of finite type. This is a square of schemes over $Y$, even though its horizontal arrows need not be $k$-linear. No assertion that $X$ or $Y$ is separated over $k$ is involved.

source.place: Sentence 1: compact-support exchange in the equivariant lift; geometry and a chosen compactification

proof.text: For the exact intrinsic finite pullbacks appearing in sfExchangeShriek, construct an equivalence for every scheme isomorphism g using pullback along its inverse. The composition and identity comparisons sfIntrinsicDerivedPullbackComp and sfIntrinsicDerivedPullbackId give the two inverse-functor isomorphisms; Equivalence.mk supplies the equivalence. Apply this to g_Y and the base-changed compactifying horizontal projection. Apply isIso_mateEquiv_of_isEquivalence_of_fullyFaithful to the two actual proper adjunctions and the specified proper pullback comparison. This proves invertibility of exactly the proper mate used in finiteExchange, with no coefficient-presentation bridge or invertibility-of-l assertion needed.

proof.text: Unfold finiteExchange, sfExchangeShriek and compactificationExchangeFromData. The canonical open exchange is already the isomorphism proEtale_openSquareExchange in these intrinsic coordinates. Its proper image, the proper mate of Step 2, and the functor associators are invertible; composition gives the finite natural isomorphism. The statement fixes c and its base change, so no compactification-independence comparison is needed.

source.place: Sentence 1: compact-support exchange in the equivariant lift; multiply the proper and open factors at finite level

proof.text: Now use an integral presentation on one of the operation/comparison domains specified in [def-exchange-projection]. For an input $K$, write $e:M\to N$ for its integral exchange, where $M=Lg_Y^*Rf_!K$ and $N=Rf_!Lg_X^*K$. Both belong to the supplied $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ domain. By the finite-reduction identifications required in that definition, reduction of the unit, square isomorphism, counit and open comparison gives exactly their finite-level counterparts. Consequently $e\otimes^L A_{E,n}$ is conjugate by those identifications to $e_n(K\otimes^L A_{E,n})$, and is invertible by Step 3 for every $n$. This uses the supplied coefficient and finite-Tor hypotheses; it asserts no additional existence or preservation of those comparison data.

source.place: Sentence 1: compact-support exchange in the equivariant lift; identify the reductions of the actual integral exchange

proof.text: For an integral-domain component e, choose a distinguished cone triangle in the ambient completed-coefficient derived category. Triangulated closure places its cone C in sfIntegralConstructible. At each positive exponent, scalarReductionDerivedExistence supplies the shift structure and triangulatedness of the actual scalarReductionDerivedExtension, so the mapped cone triangle and invertibility of the reduction of e show its third object is zero. The completeness clause of sfIntegralConstructible is IsSfDerivedComplete. Unpack its canonical Roos triangle. Exact termwise scalar restriction preserves zero objects (sfRestrictionLimits and sfRestrictionColimits), so every restricted reduction of C is zero. Product extensionality makes the identity of their product zero. The first-object zero criterion in this Roos triangle gives IsZero C; the cone-zero criterion then makes e invertible. Reflect this through the two full-subcategory inclusions with ObjectProperty.isIso_hom_iff.

source.place: Sentence 1: compact-support exchange in the equivariant lift; deduce integral invertibility from the zero reduction cones

proof.text: For $E$ coefficients the maps in [def-exchange-projection] are the rationalizations of the integral maps. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], the objects are integral representatives and the morphisms are scalar-localized integral Hom groups. Send $e$ and its inverse $v$ from Step 5 to $e\otimes1$ and $v\otimes1$; their two products are $1\otimes1$, so this is the specified rational exchange and its inverse. Naturality extends linearly to every rational morphism. For $\Qlb$ coefficients represent $K$ at a finite field $E$ and take the classes of these two inverse arrows there, using [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Composition over that common field gives both identity classes. For a morphism represented over a larger common field $L$, the scalar comparisons supplied by [def-exchange-projection] conjugate this component to the exchange at $L$. The inverse conjugates to its inverse, since if $s e=t$ with $s,t$ invertible comparison composites, the inverse equality follows by multiplication. Thus the naturality equation at $L$ gives naturality in the common-stage category, and the supplied identity/tower cocycle makes the classes independent of enlarging $L$. Finally any specified compactification identifications conjugate the displayed components by natural isomorphisms, preserving invertibility. Restricting these natural isomorphisms to any of the domains in the statement proves the assertion. No Weil structure on the underlying input, Frobenius-stable lattice, or separatedness of the two schemes has been used.

split_report.summary: Six-step proof on the exact supplied operation domains. Finite exchange is the proper mate along equivalences followed by open base change; zero reduction cones prove integral invertibility, then scalar localization and common-stage classes preserve the explicit inverse. No new nodes, no separatedness of the schemes, no coefficient-category identification and no change of statement.

Weil structure). There are no new nodes, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Step 1: hypotheses of def-exchange-projection checked with S=Y and g=g_Y as an S-morphism; b: X̄×_{Y,g_Y}Y→X̄ is an isomorphism with inverse (1,g_Y^{-1}p). Step 2: L,R,L',R',G,G',θ matched to lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences; its mate formula is exactly Ex_{*,p}, and G and G' are equivalences by lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-equivalence (scheme isomorphisms, ℓ invertible). Step 3: the upper open square is Cartesian, so β is an isomorphism by lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change, and Ex_!^c=Rp'_*(β)∘Ex_{*,p}(j_!−) is invertible; the compactification-coherence comparisons only conjugate it. Step 4 relies only on the supplied finite-reduction identifications of the definition. Step 5: the cone lies in D^b_c by the triangulated-closure lemma, so it is derived complete; exact Lπ_n^* makes its reductions zero, so the Roos triangle C→0→0 gives C=0, using the Mathlib cone leaf. Step 6: raw scalar localization and common-stage classes keep both inverse equations. Edge cases: empty X, the non-separated affine line with doubled origin with f=id, P^1→Spec k against lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso part 2, zero complexes. Not duplicates: lem-coef-frobenius-exchange-equivalence (separated schemes, E only), lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso (f=a_Y only) and lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing are special cases; the citer prop-weil-operations needs the general, non-separated Q̄_ℓ case. The statement is not weakened, and no SGA source is cited. I accept the seven declared tool_uses: lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian, lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-equivalence, lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change, prop-compactification-coherence-detailed, lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated and lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, all generic tools.
